case_title: A SRIVALLA SRINIVASA RAO & ORS. v. STATE OF A.P.
statutory_provisions: IPC s. 376 (2) (g); IPC s. 323; IPC s. 354
aggravating_circumstances: Gang rape, severe beating, delay in lodging FIR
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of Section 376(2g) and 323, acquitted of Section 354
high_court_outcome: Reduced sentence from 10 years to 7 years rigorous imprisonment
neutral_facts: The victim left her village to sell milk and was accosted by several accused on her way. They abused and beat her, then took her to a nearby field where they committed rape. Additional accused arrived and further assaulted her. The victim's cries attracted nearby villagers who found her in a traumatized state with torn clothes. She reported the incident to the police several hours after the incident, and the police collected evidence including broken glass bangles and torn clothes. The victim underwent a medical examination which indicated injuries consistent with rape, and forensic evidence confirmed the presence of semen. The prosecution argued that the delay in reporting the incident was due to the victim's trauma and that the evidence supported the occurrence of the rape.
